comparison: Both address the core biophysical gradient findings (C3, C4, C34-C38, C48-C49, C51). OpenEval finds the correlations SUPPORTED with appropriate statistics. Peer reviewers acknowledge the findings as 'timely and important' but express UNCERTAINTY about functional interpretation, questioning whether current vs. voltage threshold is more important and whether the title/abstract misleadingly suggest direct investigation of intensity sensitivity. OpenEval also notes interpretive concerns separately in R2 for C5.

Both address the functional interpretation and novelty claim (C64). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, noting correlation-to-causation leaps and that novelty cannot be independently verified. Peer reviewers similarly express UNCERTAINTY, questioning whether 'intensity sensitivity' is the best descriptor and noting the title leads readers to expect direct investigation of spontaneous rate/threshold dependency that wasn't performed.

Both address pooling of spiking and non-spiking neurons (C39-C41). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED based on ANCOVA showing no significant differences (p=0.94, p=0.71). Peer reviewers express UNCERTAINTY, requesting additional statistical tests to determine whether response latencies vary significantly with position when groups are considered separately, questioning whether pooled correlation holds independently.

Both address the statistical modeling (C52, C53, C56, C57). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with good predictive power but notes lack of independent test set validation. Peer reviewers express UNCERTAINTY, calling the VIF threshold of 4 'somewhat arbitrary' and requesting cross-validation as 'the standard and more rigorous way to prevent overfitting.' Both identify methodological limitations but OpenEval is more accepting of the approach.

Both address developmental persistence of gradients (C6, C7, C58-C60, C65-C66). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED based on correlations across ages and constant CV. Peer reviewers express UNCERTAINTY, suggesting the maturational gradient findings may overshadow 'the probably more important finding regarding the pillar/modiolar differences' and that authors should emphasize pillar/modiolar differences exist at young ages regardless of developmental trajectory.

Both address differential developmental trajectories (C61-C63). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED based on significant ANCOVA interactions (p=0.0199, p=0.0066). Peer reviewers group this with broader developmental claims and express UNCERTAINTY about emphasis, suggesting pillar/modiolar differences are more important than maturational gradients and requesting additional significance tests for age-dependent variations.

Both address morphological developmental findings (C42-C45). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with appropriate statistics (r=-0.79, p<0.0001; p=0.030). Peer reviewers also find SUPPORTED, noting the pillar/modiolar differences at young ages are 'impressive' and 'worth highlighting,' with no concerns raised about these morphological observations.

Both address fiber diameter comparisons (C46-C47). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with appropriate statistical tests (p<0.0001 for Type I vs Type II; p=0.25 for modiolar vs pillar). Peer reviewers also find SUPPORTED, raising no concerns about these morphological measurements which are consistent with previous in vivo labeling studies.

Both address basic morphological observations and classifications (C21-C25). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED based on clear anatomical criteria consistent with literature. Peer reviewers also find SUPPORTED, raising no concerns about the fiber labeling and classification methodology.

Both address firing pattern distributions (C26-C33). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with appropriate statistical tests (Welch's ANOVA, t-tests). Peer reviewers express UNCERTAINTY, questioning whether multiple comparison adjustments were made in post hoc tests and whether neurons with 'graded firing' may have 'suffered greater damage,' expressing concern about interpretation of non-spiking responses.

OpenEval R11 addresses non-significant correlation for voltage dependence of activation (C50), finding it SUPPORTED as appropriately reported negative result. Peer R1 includes C50 in broader discussion of biophysical parameters but does not specifically comment on this negative finding, focusing instead on functional interpretation concerns.
